questions.q: What three things does each StructField specify?
options: The column name, the type class, and whether nulls are allowed
Only the column name and nothing else
The file path, the delimiter, and the encoding
The row count, column count, and file size

questions.q: Why write an explicit schema instead of using inferSchema=True?
options: It skips the extra read pass inferSchema requires — Spark already knows the types before reading a single row
Explicit schemas are required by PySpark and inferSchema doesn't actually exist
It makes the file smaller on disk
There's no real benefit, it's purely stylistic
questions.explain: On a large production file, skipping that extra guessing pass is a real, measurable savings, every run.

questions.q: What does setting nullable=False on a StructField actually enforce when reading data?
options: It's mostly a hint for Spark's optimizer, not a guarantee that null values will be rejected on read
Spark validates every row and throws an error the instant it sees a null there
It automatically converts any null values in that column to zero
It deletes any row containing a null in that column
questions.explain: If the real data does contain a null there, Spark will generally still load it — the mismatch surfaces later as a bug, not an upfront read error.

questions.q: Can you use schema= and inferSchema=True together?
options: They're mutually exclusive in practice — once you supply a schema, Spark trusts it completely instead of inspecting the data
Yes, and Spark averages the two results together
Yes, inferSchema always overrides whatever schema you supply
No, using either one at all causes an immediate error
questions.explain: Supplying schema= tells Spark exactly what to expect, which is the whole point of skipping inference.

questions.q: Where does real null validation actually belong in this course?
options: Lesson 51, Null Handling — nullable=False in a schema is a signal, not a guardrail
It doesn't belong anywhere; nulls can never be checked in PySpark
Only in the CSV file itself, before it's ever read
In the StructType definition, via a validate=True flag
questions.explain: The nullable flag on a StructField is not the mechanism that actually catches or filters null values.
